summary:
# NOTES: Atalanta; or, Twelve Months in the Evening Star (Charles Napier Richards, Gutenberg #79051)

Single book, 30 chapters plus Postscript (ch. XXX). Published Brighton, H. & C. Treacher; London, Simpkin Marshall.

## Framing (Ch. I-II, Cambridge & Newbiggin)
- Maurice Sheldon (Trinity) asks about Professor Carmichael (dry scientific don; Cambridge lecturer; went to "Newbiggin-on-the-Sea", Northumberland).
- Gilbert Rice, Joe Vallance, Frank Abercromby (failed degree; uncle cut off support; packs box). Abercromby is Carmichael's pick; Carysfort (hard-headed engineer) co-builds the craft.
- Clarence Radcliffe: Oxford curate, grief. Wife May Lilian Carnforth, married after he rescued her from tramp at Chipping Norton; honeymoon at Barmouth; quarrel; she went boating with cousin Amy Vereker; boat upset near Penmaen Pool; May drowned. Radcliffe's sermon "The Wilderness". Rector unnamed.
- Radcliffe joins; Abercromby gives up his place. Jackson (Tom Jackson), Professor's servant from Elton; mother buried Elton churchyard.
- Goal: Venus, ~23-27 million miles; ship called "Asteroid". Speed 10 miles/sec. Crew: Carmichael, Carysfort, Abercromby, Radcliffe, Jackson.
- Radcliffe's theology: "Mansions of the Blest".

## Voyage (Ch. III-VI)
- Trial flight over Rothbury, Ponteland; departure 22 July, 7:30 p.m., from Newbiggin. Two letters/packets: to Home Secretary, Mayor of Newcastle. Jackson: "God save the King."
- Above Tyne; Mount Everest seen; Carmichael doubles speed. Radcliffe asks about polar regions. South Pole: Erebus and Terror, antarctic continent.
- Moon passed (~11,500 miles). Near-fall into lunar attraction; Carmichael maxes electric pressure.
- Meteoric storm from comet with fiery train (Ch. V); Carysfort prays two prayers; Radcliffe: "Work as if all depended upon yourself; pray as if all depended upon Another."
- Venus: perpetual day on one side; North Pole approached; volcano glowing near Pole; atmosphere ~500 miles deep; sun twice Earth's size. Radcliffe prays at descent. Landing at North Pole ~4 miles up.

## Northern Island (Ch. VII-VIII)
- Crater-like island, lake, cliffs; pink moss grass; waterfall; bones; Jackson shoots spindle-shaped beast, eats it; Carysfort shoots wolf-like beast that attacks Abercromby (knapsack in jaws; lost old telescope).

## Central Ocean & Southern Continent (Ch. IX-X)
- Shoreless ocean found south of island; continent with mountains; Aptaura (polar peak, 20 miles high, per Atalantans). Van Ertborn (1876), Fontana (1643) cited.
- Night attack by gorilla-like creatures with one eye each; Asteroid rises; creatures fall into river.
- Rain-mist; plateau; airship's wailing cry = "ship of death" (later explained).
- Radcliffe sees the city from cliff; tears; thinks of Lilian.

## City & Imprisonment (Ch. XI-XIII)
- Atalanta (city & land; "flowery land"); Meloria (vale); Keraunian Mountains; Karamandra = Earth ("Queen of the cold night"); Mercury = Araminta; Sun = Asti.
- Radcliffe signals with 3 rockets; two Venusians (man & woman; woman with green metal tube, blasts tree). Radcliffe lays weapon down; receives map/diagrams.
- Captured at palace terrace; bound; prison courtyard. Jackson missing (left in machine).
- Abercromby's joke: "legs run away with the heart" (cook story).
- English-letter manuscript found on table: explained later by Lilian's disguised handwriting (Ch. XXIV/XXV). Carmichael's three suppositions.
- Language lessons; Atalantan government: benevolent autocracy, crown passes sire to son/daughter for 100 years; nobility elected after; aristocracy by deeds; land state-owned.
- Royal family: King Malchon (old); daughters Melanitis (elder, queen-designate, humble) and Mexitli (younger, haughty). Cleito = commandant of palace guard.
- Jackson returns (drugged, not hypnotised per Carmichael theory; Jackson thinks mesmerised).
- Trial in Hall of Perfect Justice (Ch. XIII): Professor says 1,200 million people on Earth. Mexitli: Christianity testimony; Radcliffe describes the Crucifixion: "God is Love." Melanitis: "I should not wonder if they killed Him." Radcliffe: "I have." Mexitli spares Radcliffe for a year; others death sentence conditional. Malchon: "Make the Prince King" is Lydon's later quote, not here.
- Second Ordeal (Ch. XIV): Abercromby's insult ("diplomatist... mind left in cloak-room"); Mexitli sentences him to two months' prison. Radcliffe's love for Lilian is "dead and buried," churchyard near Chipping Norton.

## Mayana & Cleophon; Malchon's Gospel (Ch. XV-XVI)
- Mayana (Cleophon's wife, cousin of princesses), sister Minya. Story of Melanitis' sun-fever and amnesia, Malchon's rash prayer at Temple of the Sun on lake-island.
- Malchon's history: a stranger ("the Prince") came over Keraunian Hills; built road; crucified-like elsewhere; told Atalanteans He would return.
- New Testament (Luke & Acts) transcribed into Atalantan by scribes.
- Lydon (high priest of Sun/Asti); Parmenton (rebel), Mauro Katakalon (two names), Medon.

## Festival & Rebellion (Ch. XVII-XIX)
- Abercromby freed; sees rebel meeting in house; Radcliffe preaches and is rebuked.
- Festival of Panacla (Ch. XVIII): Lydon offers incense; Radcliffe knocks vessel from Carmichael's hand; Abercromby and Jackson hit guards; rain-mist covers; Radcliffe clubbed.
- Radcliffe wakes with Melanitis: recalls Tenby, Lilian, Pont Aberglaslyn. Melanitis knows private details.
- Aerial voyage (Ch. XIX): Melandria island; Minola (Mexitli's maid); Amarilla (old matron, Ayacatil and Andron later).
- Island of Twilight (Ch. XX): governor Andron, wife Ayacatil; "How Keraunion Died" song.
- Aptaura Observatory (Ch. XXI-XXII): three scientists; earth visible as green-red star.
- Abercromby's reveal: Lilian is alive as Melanitis; Abercromby tells Radcliffe. "Solitude" song triggers Melanitis's faint.
- Lydon's revolt (Ch. XXIII): arsenal explosion; Malchon fights; Tom fights, dies; Lydon captured. Rebels Parmenton, Medon captured.

## Denunciation & Retribution (Ch. XXIV-XXV)
- Lydon's private trial in King's chamber: exposes Melanitis as Lilian (Karamandran soul in Atalantan body). Lilian & Radcliffe embrace; Lydon attacks; Malchon shields Radcliffe/Melanitis, killed with sacrificial knife; he says "Let the Prince be King."
- Minola kills Lydon with pistol (avenging her father Marcon).
- Mexitli Queen; Melanitis renounces throne, becomes ruler of Melandria. Cleito and Arniphon taken back to Earth.
- Melanitis=Lilian's account of soul transference (Lydon's vision).

## Burial, Tom's Death, Farewell (Ch. XXVI-XXIX)
- Procession to Pass of Amalona ("Bridge of the Tear"). Dead cremated (dishonoured). "Farewell of Amalona" chant.
- Temple search (Ch. XXVII): serpent in grove; priest Talmon killed by Minola; Tom found alive behind wall in Temple, dies; "Glory Song"; "Christ will just send a chariot"; mother at Elton. Green flagstone under altar; Radcliffe nearly killed by beast in cave.
- Tom buried; epitaph verse (Ch. XXVIII). Malchon's manuscript scroll found (Calchon, Ixtilon).
- Mexitli's terms: Earth-travellers must keep Atalanta secret; Carmichael/Carysfort return to Earth ~20th of Cayamarca, 55 days; start 5 days before.
- Abercromby engaged to Minya.
- Feast of Farewell (Ch. XXIX): Radcliffe marries Melanitis; Queen's speech; "Waiting for the Light" song; departure from Aptaura, signal from Atalanta to Karamandra.

## POSTSCRIPT (Ch. XXX)
- Narrators: Maurice Sheldon and Gilbert Rice. Walking tour Cornwall (Bude, Boscastle, Tintagel, Wadebridge, St Breock Downs, Newquay). Aerolite falls near St Breock; cylinder with manuscripts found; opened with hammer and chisel at St Columb hotel.
- Two theories: destroyed in space by meteorite; or returned to Venus.
- Professor Rossini (Italian observatory): flashes from Venus's southern peak counted matching letters in "Carmichael" and "Carysfort."
